about: Settings measured as a loss (LAUNCHER-1225 step 2, idea from the scout's planner study). The auto-tune never tries a row's setting inside its scope (the planner does not read this list yet); when the user sets one, the launcher says what was measured and runs it anyway (the user's flags win). Each row names its evidence; one-run rows are forecasts. A row is removed only by a new measurement that beats it.

answer_classes.about: LAUNCHER-1225 step 2 (main 2026-11-18; critic of 59abd70): what a setting does to the answers. exact = same answers as the plan without it (memory locking, how the file is loaded, the context size, records); placement = the same maths run in another place or order (where weights sit, batch size, slots, threads): speed, and possibly last-bit float differences, NOT shown token-identical; quality = can change tokens on purpose: the auto-tune may pick it on its own only when its quality-gate row in TOKEN_MODES (bin/moe_cache_approx.py) has status 'won' (the gate passed and the speed win was measured); a setting missing from this table counts as quality without a gate (never picked on its own). Keys: auto-tune dimensions and plan-file setting names. planner/never_list.py BUILTIN_CLASSES holds the same table for when this file cannot be read.
